imagem.definicao: The ready-made package with the program and everything it needs to run (libraries, files, default configuration).
imagem.vidaReal: A prefab module: it always leaves the factory the same and arrives at the construction site ready to go.
imagem.limite: The image doesn’t change once it’s built. To change it, you build another version (another tag).

conteiner.definicao: A program running from an image, isolated from the other programs on the machine.
conteiner.vidaReal: The prefab module installed and working.
conteiner.limite: Several containers come out of the same image at the same time, and each one can die and be replaced in seconds.

registry.definicao: The server images are downloaded from (Docker Hub, registry.k8s.io, ghcr.io...).
registry.vidaReal: The factory and warehouse for prefab parts.
registry.limite: A registry can be private: then you need a password (imagePullSecrets) to download.

tag.definicao: The image’s version label, after the colon.
tag.vidaReal: The model or batch of the prefab part (v1, v2).
tag.limite: “latest” doesn’t mean “the newest”: it’s just a tag like any other, and it can change without warning.

cluster.definicao: The set of machines (nodes) managed by Kubernetes, plus the control plane that runs them.
cluster.vidaReal: A condo: several buildings and a management office.
cluster.limite: In a cluster the “buildings” (nodes) are identical, replaceable machines; nobody lives in a specific node.

control-plane.definicao: The components that make decisions and store the cluster’s state: API Server, etcd, scheduler and controller manager.
control-plane.limite: In a managed cluster (EKS, GKE, AKS) you don’t even see the management office: the provider takes care of it.

api-server.definicao: The cluster’s front door: it receives every request (from kubectl and from the components themselves), checks it and saves it.
api-server.vidaReal: The doorman (Apolinário): every request goes through him.
api-server.limite: It doesn’t run anything by itself: it only records; the ones who act are the controllers and the kubelet.
api-server.exemplo: kubectl get pods  (a request to the API Server)

etcd.definicao: The key-value database where the cluster stores all its objects.
etcd.vidaReal: The management office’s record book (Etelvina, the archivist).
etcd.limite: Losing etcd means losing the cluster’s memory: that’s why it has backups and replicas.

scheduler.definicao: Chooses which node each new pod will run on, based on space, rules and preferences.
scheduler.vidaReal: The real-estate agent (Shirley): she finds a building with room for each new apartment.
scheduler.limite: She only chooses once. After the pod is born, it never changes nodes; if the node goes down, another pod is born.
scheduler.exemplo: Events: Scheduled  Successfully assigned default/web to node-1

controller.definicao: A loop that compares the desired state (spec) with the actual one (status) and fixes the difference, nonstop.
controller.vidaReal: The inspector (Conceição): she compares the blueprint with the construction and orders fixes.
controller.limite: It doesn’t do everything at once: it fixes one step, looks again, fixes another.

kubelet.definicao: The agent on each node that creates and watches over the containers of that node’s pods.
kubelet.vidaReal: The building’s caretaker (Kleber): he looks after the apartments in his building.
kubelet.limite: If the kubelet stops, the node becomes NotReady; 5 minutes later, only pods with an owner (Deployment, StatefulSet) are reborn on other nodes.

node.definicao: A machine (physical or virtual) in the cluster, where pods run.
node.vidaReal: A building in the condo, with power (CPU) and space (memory).
node.limite: Nodes are alike and replaceable: there’s no “main building”.

pod.definicao: The smallest unit in Kubernetes: one or more containers that share the same network (IP) and the same volumes, always on the same node.
pod.vidaReal: An apartment: it has its own address, and whoever lives there shares the space.
pod.limite: A broken apartment isn’t repaired: the pod is replaced by another one, with another name and another IP.

kubectl.definicao: The command line for talking to the cluster.
kubectl.vidaReal: The intercom to the front gate.
kubectl.limite: It only talks to the front gate (API Server), never directly to the buildings or the apartments.

manifesto.definicao: The file that describes an object: apiVersion, kind, metadata and spec.
manifesto.vidaReal: The blueprint: it says how you want things to end up, not how to get there.
manifesto.limite: A blueprint doesn’t guarantee the construction: the object can be rejected (wrong field) or get stuck (an image that doesn’t exist).

declarativo.definicao: Declarative: you describe the desired state and the cluster gets there. Imperative: you give every order yourself.
declarativo.vidaReal: Handing over the blueprint × giving orders brick by brick.
declarativo.limite: The two live side by side: commands like kubectl scale are imperative, but they change the desired state the controllers chase.

reconciliacao.definicao: The cycle of looking at the actual state, comparing it with the desired one and acting to bring the two closer.
reconciliacao.vidaReal: The thermostat: it compares the temperature with the one you want and turns the AC on or off.
reconciliacao.limite: A thermostat has a single sensor; Kubernetes has dozens of controllers, each one looking after one type of object.
reconciliacao.exemplo: Deleted a pod from a Deployment? Another one is born on its own.

namespace.definicao: A logical division of the cluster: names are unique inside it.
namespace.vidaReal: A company that rents apartments in several buildings; each company can have its own “meeting-room”.
namespace.limite: On its own, a namespace doesn’t isolate the network or limit resources: for that there’s NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota.

label.definicao: Key=value tags on objects, and the rule that picks objects by their tags.
label.vidaReal: Tags on the door (“team: support”) and “everyone with tag X”.
label.limite: Labels aren’t unique: two objects with the same tag get picked together, like it or not.

sidecar.definicao: A helper container in the same pod as the main one (logs, proxy, sync). Today the right way is the native one: in initContainers, with restartPolicy: Always (level 5).
sidecar.vidaReal: The roommate who helps out the main tenant.
sidecar.limite: It’s born and dies with the pod: you can’t scale the assistant separately from the main tenant. Written as a regular container, it doesn’t know when to leave, and a Job with it never finishes.

replicaset.definicao: Keeps a number of identical pods running: it creates the missing ones and deletes the extras.
replicaset.limite: It only checks the count and the labels: if a stray pod has the same labels, it gets “adopted”.

deployment.definicao: Manages ReplicaSets to swap the pods’ version a little at a time (rolling update) and lets you go back (rollback).
deployment.vidaReal: A renovation in stages: it swaps one apartment at a time, without closing the condo, and it can be undone.
deployment.limite: Without a readinessProbe, Kubernetes thinks “started” means “ready”: a version that crashes after a few seconds makes it through the renovation.

rolling-update.definicao: The limits of the gradual swap: how many extra pods can exist and how many can be unavailable during the swap.
rolling-update.vidaReal: How many extra temporary apartments can open / how many can be closed during the renovation.
rolling-update.limite: The API rejects both at zero: the swap would never move. If a percentage rounds down to zero (maxSurge: 0 and maxUnavailable: 10% of 3 pods), Kubernetes uses 1.

recreate.definicao: The strategy that deletes all the old pods before creating the new ones.
recreate.vidaReal: Closing the whole condo to renovate it.
recreate.limite: There’s a stretch of time with no one serving: use it only when two versions can’t run together.

rollback.definicao: Taking the Deployment back to an earlier revision of the template.
rollback.vidaReal: Undoing the renovation and going back to the old design.
rollback.limite: Only the pod template goes back: deleted data or database migrations don’t come back.

service.definicao: A fixed address (IP and DNS name) for a group of pods picked by labels, which spreads the connections among them.
service.vidaReal: The company’s fixed phone extension: people move between apartments, the extension stays.
service.limite: The extension only rings in apartments that are ready (readiness); if none is ready, the call is refused.

endpoints.definicao: The current list of IPs and ports of the ready pods behind a Service.
endpoints.vidaReal: The list of apartments behind the phone extension.
endpoints.limite: It changes all the time, on its own: never write pod IPs by hand.

kube-proxy.definicao: The program on each node that makes the Service IP work: it writes the node’s network rules (iptables or nftables) that send each connection to one of the ready pods.
kube-proxy.vidaReal: Each building’s phone technician: wires things up so a call to the extension rings at one of the apartments that answer.
kube-proxy.limite: He doesn’t sit in the middle of the call: he only leaves the wires ready (kernel rules), and the kernel forwards each call. With some network plugins (like Cilium) there’s no technician at all: the plugin does the job.

nodeport.definicao: A Service that opens the same port (30000–32767) on every node.
nodeport.vidaReal: A numbered intercom at the door of every building.
nodeport.limite: It’s a high port, exposed on every node: great for testing, bad for production.

loadbalancer.definicao: A Service that asks the cloud provider for a load balancer with an external IP.
loadbalancer.vidaReal: The street-side front gate, with turnstiles that spread people out.
loadbalancer.limite: Outside the cloud (kind, minikube) the external IP stays <pending> without some extra help (MetalLB, cloud-provider-kind). Here the simulator plays that role, like cloud-provider-kind does, and the IP shows up.

port-forward.definicao: A temporary tunnel, opened by kubectl, from a port on your computer to a pod (or to a Service, which picks a pod).
port-forward.vidaReal: A temporary passage from your house straight to an apartment, without going through the front gate.
port-forward.limite: The passage goes to a single pod (picked when it opens), only you use it, and it disappears when the command stops: it’s for testing, not for serving customers.

headless.definicao: A Service with no IP of its own (clusterIP: None): the DNS name returns the IP of each ready pod. It’s what gives each pod in a StatefulSet its name (db-0.db).
headless.vidaReal: Instead of the main extension, a list with each clerk’s direct extension.
headless.limite: Without a Service IP, nobody picks a clerk at random: the caller picks the pod (and has to deal with pods that come and go).

dns.definicao: Every Service gets a name: service.namespace.svc.cluster.local.
dns.vidaReal: The full address: name, company, neighborhood and city.
dns.limite: Within the same namespace the short name is enough; from another namespace, you need the name with the namespace.

coredns.definicao: The cluster’s name server: a Deployment in kube-system, behind the kube-dns Service, that answers each pod with the IP of the name it asked for.
coredns.vidaReal: The condo’s switchboard operator: you say the company’s name, she gives you the extension number.
coredns.limite: She only gives out the number, she doesn’t complete the call: if the extension doesn’t answer, it’s not her fault. And whoever knows the IP by heart can call even without her.

ingress.definicao: HTTP rules (host and path) that take traffic from outside to the Services, through a controller.
ingress.limite: The most widely used controller, ingress-nginx, was retired in 2026; the new way is the Gateway API.

gateway-api.definicao: The evolution of Ingress: Gateway (the entrance, run by the platform) and HTTPRoute (each team’s rules).
gateway-api.vidaReal: The condo’s front gate (run by the management office), with a sign for each company.
gateway-api.limite: They’re new resources (CRDs) and need an implementation installed in the cluster.

configmap.definicao: Plain-text settings that pods use as environment variables or files.
configmap.limite: Changing the ConfigMap doesn’t change the variables of a pod that’s already running: the pod has to be restarted.

secret.definicao: Sensitive data (passwords, tokens) that pods use as variables or files.
secret.limite: It’s an envelope, not a safe: the content is only base64, which anyone can decode. Real protection comes from RBAC and encryption in etcd.

base64.definicao: A way to write any data using only letters, numbers, + and /. It’s how Secrets store their values.
base64.vidaReal: Writing the password in Morse code: it gets in the way of a quick glance, but anyone with the chart can decode it.
base64.limite: It’s not encryption: it’s for storing binary data as text, not for protecting it. Whoever reads the Secret reads the password.

volume.definicao: A folder that a pod’s containers mount (volumeMounts). The type says where the content comes from: empty (emptyDir), a ConfigMap, a Secret or a disk (PVC).
volume.vidaReal: A cabinet installed in the apartment: it can come empty, with the notices from the bulletin board, or with the things from the storage unit in the garage.
volume.limite: Mounting over a folder hides what the image had there: nginx’s default page disappears when the ConfigMap takes its place.

emptydir.definicao: An empty volume that’s born with the pod and deleted along with it.
emptydir.vidaReal: The work desk: it’s gone in the move.
emptydir.limite: It survives a container restart, but not the pod being replaced.

pv-pvc.definicao: The PV is a piece of the cluster’s disk; the PVC is a pod’s request for a disk (size and access mode).
pv-pvc.vidaReal: The storage unit in the garage and the request to rent it.
pv-pvc.limite: A ReadWriteOnce disk mounts on only one node at a time: two pods on different nodes don’t share the same storage unit.

storageclass.definicao: The kind of disk (fast, cheap...) and who creates it when a PVC asks for one.
storageclass.vidaReal: The kind of storage unit: climate-controlled or regular.
storageclass.limite: Without a default StorageClass, a PVC with no class stays Pending forever.

statefulset.definicao: Like a Deployment, but each pod has a fixed name (db-0, db-1) and its own disk.
statefulset.vidaReal: Numbered apartments (101, 102...), each one always with the same storage unit.
statefulset.limite: A fixed name isn’t a fixed IP: the db-0 pod can come back with another IP, but with the same DNS name.

daemonset.definicao: Ensures one pod on every node (or on the chosen nodes).
daemonset.vidaReal: The fire extinguisher: one in every building, including the ones built later.
daemonset.limite: It has no “replicas”: the number of pods is the number of nodes.

job.definicao: Runs pods until a number of them finish successfully, then stops.
job.vidaReal: A one-off construction job: the facade got painted, done.
job.limite: If the program fails, the Job tries again up to the backoffLimit; after that it gives up.

cronjob.definicao: Creates a Job at scheduled times (cron syntax).
cronjob.vidaReal: Trash pickup every Tuesday at 7 a.m.
cronjob.limite: The time is the cluster’s clock (usually UTC), not yours: for another time zone, set timeZone (e.g. America/Sao_Paulo).

init-container.definicao: A container that runs and finishes before the main ones start.
init-container.vidaReal: The painting crew that gets the apartment ready before the move-in.
init-container.limite: If it fails, the pod doesn’t leave Init: the main containers don’t even start.

sidecar-nativo.definicao: An init container with restartPolicy: Always: it starts before the app, keeps running beside it and exits when the app finishes.
sidecar-nativo.vidaReal: The assistant who works alongside the resident: arrives before, stays all day and leaves when the resident goes out.
sidecar-nativo.limite: A sidecar written as a regular container never finishes, and a Job with it never becomes Complete.

backofflimit.definicao: How many failures a Job accepts before giving up. Between one attempt and the next, the wait doubles (10s, 20s, 40s...).
backofflimit.vidaReal: The bricklayer comes back to try again, a little later each time, until the contract says “enough”.
backofflimit.limite: Trying again doesn’t fix a mistake in the command: read the log before raising the limit.

liveness.definicao: A periodic “is the program alive?” check. If it fails, the kubelet restarts the container.
liveness.vidaReal: The building manager knocks on the door: “you alive?” If nobody answers, restart.
liveness.limite: A check that’s too strict restarts a program that’s just slow, and makes the problem worse.

readiness.definicao: A periodic “can it take traffic?” check. While it fails, the pod is taken out of the Service’s endpoints.
readiness.vidaReal: “Ready for visitors yet?” Until it is, the phone extension sends nobody over.
readiness.limite: Readiness doesn’t restart anything: a pod can stay “not ready” forever, still running.

startup.definicao: A “has it finished starting up?” check. Until it passes, the other checks wait.
startup.vidaReal: The deadline for the move: until then, nobody chases you.
startup.limite: It only counts at the start; once it passes, it doesn’t run again.

requests.definicao: The minimum CPU and memory reserved for the container; the scheduler only places the pod where that fits.
requests.vidaReal: The contracted power: it only goes to a building where it fits.
requests.limite: Reserving isn’t using: a pod can reserve a lot and use little, and the space sits idle.

limits.definicao: The maximum CPU and memory. Go over the memory limit and the container is killed (OOMKilled); over the CPU limit, it gets slow.
limits.vidaReal: The circuit breaker (memory) and reduced water pressure (CPU).
limits.limite: The circuit breaker trips the container, not the whole pod: it restarts and can go down again (CrashLoopBackOff).

hpa.definicao: Raises and lowers the replicas on its own, based on usage (CPU, memory or custom metrics).
hpa.vidaReal: Hiring temp staff for Black Friday and letting them go afterward.
hpa.limite: It needs requests set and metrics in the cluster; without them, it does nothing.

oomkilled.definicao: The container went over limits.memory and the kernel killed it (exit code 137). It restarts, and goes into CrashLoopBackOff if it keeps happening.
oomkilled.vidaReal: The circuit breaker that trips when too many appliances are switched on at once.
oomkilled.limite: Raising the limit only helps if the program really needs that much; if it leaks memory, it just delays the next crash.

qos.definicao: Guaranteed (requests = limits), Burstable (something declared) or BestEffort (nothing): the order of who goes first when the node runs out of memory.
qos.vidaReal: Whoever contracted guaranteed power is the last to lose electricity during rationing.
qos.limite: It doesn’t protect a pod from its own limit: a Guaranteed pod that goes over limits.memory dies just the same.

metrics-server.definicao: The component that measures CPU and memory for pods and nodes. kubectl top and the HPA’s numbers come from it.
metrics-server.vidaReal: The meter reader who checks each apartment’s meter.
metrics-server.limite: It doesn’t come installed in kind (or in many clusters): without it, “Metrics API not available”. And it only keeps the present, not the history.

resourcequota.definicao: A namespace’s ceiling: how many pods, and how much requests and limits added up.
resourcequota.vidaReal: Each company’s power quota in the condo.
resourcequota.limite: It counts what’s declared, not what’s used: and, with a CPU or memory quota, every container must declare requests and limits.

limitrange.definicao: Per-container rules in a namespace: default requests and limits for anyone who declared nothing, plus minimums and maximums.
limitrange.vidaReal: The default consumption label the management office puts on anyone who arrives without one.
limitrange.limite: It only applies to pods created afterward: whoever was already running doesn’t get the label.

taint.definicao: A taint marks a node to repel pods; a toleration lets a pod go there anyway.
taint.vidaReal: A restricted building: only people with authorization get in.
taint.limite: A toleration allows, it doesn’t force: to send the pod there, use nodeSelector or affinity.

affinity.definicao: Rules for choosing which nodes the pod must (required) or prefers to (preferred) run on, by the nodes’ labels.
affinity.vidaReal: “I want a building with a generator.”
affinity.limite: A required rule that no node meets leaves the pod Pending forever; and the rule only counts on arrival: it doesn’t remove whoever already lives there.

drain.definicao: cordon: the node stops receiving new pods. drain: on top of that, it removes the pods already on it.
drain.vidaReal: Closing off the building to new residents / emptying the building for the renovation.
drain.limite: A standalone pod (no Deployment or ReplicaSet) deleted by drain doesn’t come back anywhere.

pdb.definicao: How many pods in a group must stay ready (minAvailable) or may leave (maxUnavailable) during maintenance. drain respects it: with no slack, it waits.
pdb.vidaReal: “At least 2 elevators working”, even during maintenance.
pdb.limite: It only applies to whoever evicts through the API (drain, node autoscaler): it doesn’t protect against a node going down, a bug or kubectl delete.

antiafinidade.definicao: A rule for a pod to stay away from other pods (picked by labels): on another node, or in another zone, depending on the topologyKey.
antiafinidade.vidaReal: Not keeping both backup copies in the same building.
antiafinidade.limite: When required, it leaves the extra replica Pending if there aren’t enough buildings. For “separate them if you can”, use preferred.

espalhamento.definicao: Spreads a group’s pods across nodes or zones, with a maximum difference (maxSkew) between the fullest and the emptiest domain.
espalhamento.vidaReal: Spreading a chain’s stores across neighborhoods, without packing one and leaving another empty.
espalhamento.limite: Tainted nodes count as an empty domain: in kind, with topologyKey hostname, the control plane leaves replicas Pending.

priorityclass.definicao: An importance number for pods. When there’s no room, the scheduler removes lower-priority pods to place the more important one.
priorityclass.vidaReal: The ambulance that cuts the line (and moves the parked car out of the spot).
priorityclass.limite: Whoever gets removed really leaves: without a Deployment behind it, it doesn’t come back; with one, it goes back in line (Pending).

node-notready.definicao: The node stopped reporting in (kubelet stopped, network or machine down). About 5 minutes later, its pods are evicted.
node-notready.vidaReal: A power outage in the building.
node-notready.limite: The downed node’s pods stay “Terminating” until it comes back: only the ones with an owner (Deployment, StatefulSet) are reborn somewhere else.

rbac.definicao: The Role says what can be done; the RoleBinding gives that permission to someone.
rbac.vidaReal: The type of badge / handing the badge to someone.
rbac.limite: There’s no “deny” in RBAC: everything starts denied and the rules only allow.

serviceaccount.definicao: The identity of a program (pod) inside the cluster.
serviceaccount.vidaReal: A machine’s badge (the elevator’s, the cameras’).
serviceaccount.limite: Every pod uses one (the “default”), even if you don’t ask for it.

networkpolicy.definicao: Rules for who can connect to whom, between pods.
networkpolicy.limite: With no policy at all, everything is open; and a policy only works if the cluster’s network plugin implements it.

clusterrole.definicao: The badge that’s valid across the whole cluster (ClusterRole) and handing it to someone in every namespace (ClusterRoleBinding). Some come ready-made: view, edit, admin and cluster-admin.
clusterrole.vidaReal: The master badge, which opens the doors of every block.
clusterrole.limite: A RoleBinding that points to a ClusterRole only counts in its own namespace: to count in all of them, it has to be a ClusterRoleBinding.

securitycontext.definicao: The security options of the pod and of each container: which user it runs as (runAsUser, runAsNonRoot), whether the disk is read-only and what powers the program has.
securitycontext.vidaReal: Nobody gets the master key (root): each resident uses the key to their own apartment.
securitycontext.limite: It limits the damage if the program is broken into, but it doesn’t fix the program: a flaw is still there, just with less power.

pod-security.definicao: The rules a namespace imposes on pods, by label: privileged, baseline or restricted, in enforce (rejects) or warn (warns) mode.
pod-security.limite: In a namespace with enforce, the Deployment is created (with just a Warning), but the pods are rejected: the symptom is READY 0/1 and the reason is in the ReplicaSet.

events.definicao: Records of what happened to each object (scheduled, image pulled, failed...).
events.limite: They disappear after an hour: look right away.

logs.definicao: What the container’s program wrote to its output.
logs.limite: If the container restarted, the previous diary is in --previous; the one before that is already lost.

crashloopbackoff.definicao: The container crashes right after starting, and the kubelet waits longer and longer to restart it (10s, 20s, 40s... up to 5 min).
crashloopbackoff.vidaReal: The resident faints every time they walk in, and the building manager waits longer and longer before trying again.
crashloopbackoff.limite: It’s not an error in itself: it’s the symptom. The cause is in the logs (--previous) and in describe.

imagepullbackoff.definicao: The kubelet couldn’t pull the image and is waiting to try again.
imagepullbackoff.vidaReal: The prefab module never arrived: the order had the wrong model.
imagepullbackoff.limite: It could be the name, the tag, a private registry without a password, or a download limit.

pending.definicao: The pod exists but isn’t running yet: no node (FailedScheduling) or waiting for something (a volume, an image).
pending.vidaReal: Waiting in the lobby: no building has room or authorization.
pending.limite: Pending can last forever if no node fits: the reason is in the Events.

createcontainerconfigerror.definicao: The kubelet can’t put together the container’s configuration: a ConfigMap or Secret (or one of its keys) is missing, or runAsNonRoot doesn’t match the image.
createcontainerconfigerror.vidaReal: The move got stuck at the door: the envelope with the password (or the bulletin board) the resident needs never arrived.
createcontainerconfigerror.limite: As soon as what’s missing shows up, the kubelet tries again on its own: no need to delete the pod.

helm.definicao: A package manager: a chart is a template of manifests; the values.yaml picks the options.
helm.vidaReal: The builder’s standard design; the values.yaml is the finishes you pick.
helm.limite: The chart hides the manifests: when something breaks, you still need to read the generated YAML (helm template).

release.definicao: An installation of a chart, with a name and a history: each upgrade or rollback is a new revision.
release.vidaReal: A job the builder delivered, with a record of every renovation.
release.limite: The history lives in Secrets in the namespace (sh.helm.release.v1...): delete the Secrets and Helm forgets the job, while the objects stay there, ownerless.

kustomize.definicao: Builds variations of manifests (dev, prod) from a base, without templates.
kustomize.vidaReal: The same blueprint with adjustments for each city.
kustomize.limite: It only applies changes on top of the base: it has no logic (ifs and loops) like Helm does.

overlay.definicao: The base has the shared YAML; each overlay points to the base and lists only that environment’s adjustments (namespace, replicas, image, patches).
overlay.vidaReal: The headquarters’ blueprint and each branch’s sheet of adjustments.
overlay.limite: An overlay can’t see variables or conditions: it only merges and swaps fields. Real logic calls for Helm.

gitops.definicao: Git holds the desired state, and a tool (Argo CD, Flux) applies it and fixes the cluster on its own.
gitops.vidaReal: The blueprint filed at the notary, with an inspector who sets the construction straight on his own.
gitops.limite: A change made directly in the cluster gets undone by the inspector: the way is always through Git.

crd-operator.definicao: A CRD creates a new type of object in the API; the Operator is the controller that knows how to take care of it.
crd-operator.vidaReal: A new form at the management office / the specialist who knows how to handle it.
crd-operator.limite: On its own, the CRD only stores the form: without the Operator, nothing happens.
